summary: Royall Tyler is a scholar of Japanology. He studied at Harvard University and Columbia University under Donald Keene. He held teaching posts at Wisconsin-Madison, Oslo, and Ohio State, headed the Japan Centre at ANU (1990–2000), and visited Harvard (2001–2002).
Royce Wiles works in the field of Indology. He completed his PhD at the Australian National University by 2000 and held an academic post there.

Ruben L. F. Habito works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Ateneo de Manila, Sophia University, and the University of Tokyo under Akira Hirakawa and Jikidō Takasaki. He held posts at Sophia, Ryukoku, and Southern Methodist University (1989).
Rudolf Geiger studied at Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg from 1912 to 1914. He later held an academic post at the University of Munich from around 1937 to 1962.

Rudolf Haym worked in philosophy and history. He studied at Köllnisches Gymnasium, Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg, and Frederick William University Berlin. He later served on the faculty at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg in 1868.

Rudolf Kaschewsky specialized in Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Cologne and the University of Bonn, where he later served as Akademischer Rat from 1974 to 2004. He also taught Tibetan at Goethe University Frankfurt.
Rudolf Lange was a scholar of Japanology and linguistics. He held academic posts at the University of Tokyo from around 1874 to 1881 and at Humboldt University of Berlin from around 1887 to 1922.
Rudolf Much was a scholar in linguistics, history, and archaeology. He completed his studies at the University of Vienna between 1883 and 1887 and later held a post there from around 1895 to 1936.

Rudolf Otto worked in religious studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg and under Richard von Garbe, and held academic posts at the University of Breslau (~1914–1917) and the University of Marburg (~1917–1929).
Rudolf Seydel worked in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Leipzig University from 1852 to 1856 and subsequently held a post there from around 1860 to 1892.

Rudolf Thurneysen was a linguist who studied at Leipzig University and under Heinrich Zimmer. He held academic posts at the University of Jena (~1882–1887), the University of Freiburg (~1887–1913), and the University of Bonn (~1913–1923).

Rudolf von Roth specialized in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Tübinger Stift under Heinrich Ewald and with Eugène Burnouf. He spent his career at the University of Tübingen, serving as Privatdozent from 1845 and Extraordinarius from 1848 to 1895.

Rudrapatna Shamasastry was an Indologist educated at the University of Madras, Sri Chamarajendra Sanskrit College, Oriental University, and the University of Calcutta. He served as Principal of Sri Chamarajendra Sanskrit College (1912–1918) and Curator of Oriental Research Institute Mysore (1918–1929).

Ruixuan Chen works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied under Jens-Uwe Hartmann, Paul Harrison, and others, earning a PhD from Leiden University (attested 2018), and holds a post at Heidelberg University.

Rulon Wells worked in linguistics, philosophy, and Indology. He completed his studies at the University of Utah (1935–1939) and Harvard University (1939–1942) before serving on the faculty at Yale University from around 1945 to 1989.

Rupert Gethin specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Manchester under Lance S. Cousins. Since 1987, he has held posts at the University of Bristol, and he became President of the Pali Text Society in 2003.

Ruriko Sakuma is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. She was educated at Nagoya University and held an appointment as a full-time researcher and director at the Eastern Institute (attested 2015).
Rustam Sabirov specializes in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He received his doctorate in history from Moscow State University in 2004, where he also held a post as a senior researcher.

Ruth Fuller Sasaki worked in Buddhist studies and Japanology. She studied at the University of Chicago and under D.T. Suzuki, Sokei-an, Zuigan Goto, and Mukai Kono. She directed the Buddhist Society of America and served as abbess of Ryosen-an.

Ruth Gamble works in Tibetology and history/archaeology. She completed her PhD at the Australian National University under John Powers, Roger Jackson, and David Templeman. She has held posts at the Australian National University and the University of Munich (attested 2016).
